# BASELINE — before R1 (7874dde)

Frozen. Captured from a git worktree at `7874dde` — the commit before the coverage rule — so
these are the **real** pre-change rule's numbers, not a reimplementation.

Valid only for the fixtures that produced them. Recapture whenever `turns.json` or
`catalog.json` changes:

```
git worktree add /tmp/rb 7874dde
cp src/core/tests/fixtures/{turns,catalog}.json /tmp/rb/src/core/tests/fixtures/
# in the worktree: make IntentGraph::observe_live pub(crate), add
# ToolRegistry::with_embedder_for_test, register `#[cfg(test)] mod harness;` in lib.rs,
# and copy src/core/src/harness.rs with the after-only parts removed (dense_verdict,
# Coverage, cohesion, the policy sweep, the projection guard, embed_query_batch_with_identity).
cargo test -p ratel-ai-core --lib harness_baseline -- --ignored --nocapture
```

Coverage, cohesion and the policy sweep are absent by construction — they are quantities only
the post-change rule has. Comparable: cluster shape, purity, merge quality, served top-k.

Generated by `cargo test -p ratel-ai-core --lib harness_report -- --ignored`.
Fixtures: `turns.json` (50 turns, 47 distinct queries), `catalog.json` (26 ops).

**Absolute numbers mean little — only deltas between runs on this fixture do.** One
embedding model, two domains, labels assigned by one person, and the same turns both
build and evaluate the graph, so this measures whether a change altered behaviour, not
whether it generalises.

Compare against `harness-baseline.md`, the frozen pre-R1 capture, by diffing the two
files. Nothing here restates those numbers: a hardcoded summary goes stale the moment
the fixtures change, and says so silently.
